hook: You opened Claude, typed one line, got a stranger's paragraph back, and closed the tab.
body:
The tool wasn't the problem. Nobody showed you the setup: your pricing, your voice and your clients, written down once, before you type a word.

Stop hunting for a better prompt. Write the one page Claude reads first.

hook: Skip the prompt engineering course.
body:
You don't need clever phrasing. You need to brief Claude the way you'd brief a sharp new hire: who you serve, what good looks like, what you'd never say.

Most owners aren't missing a technique. They're missing the habit of giving context.

hook: There's 1 task in your week that shouldn't exist.
body:
Not delegate. Delete.

Drop it in the comments. I'll reply to as many as I can with how Claude could take the first pass at it.
old_hook: Name 1 task you'd delete from your week if you could.

hook: Re-explaining your business every chat is the most expensive habit in AI.
body:
Write it down once. 1 page: who you serve, how you sound, 3 things you'd never say, 1 example of your best work.

Put it in a Claude Project's instructions and every chat in that project starts with it. Your drafts stop sounding like everyone else's.
old_hook: Stop re-explaining your business to Claude every chat.

hook: 5 signs AI is adding work to your week instead of removing it.
body:
1. 6 tabs of "AI tools to try" open
2. 40 saved prompts you've never used
3. Every chat starts from zero
4. You judged Claude on 1 bad answer
5. You feel behind everyone online

3 or more? You don't need more AI. You need less, set up once.

hook: Your Claude answers are generic because you ask too fast.
body:
Add 1 line before your request: "Ask me 5 questions before you answer."

Claude stops guessing and works from what you need. Slower start, better first draft.

hook: Her 75-page guide was from last year. The update took one evening.
body:
Shannon runs an online shop. Her words: "Heidi had the new version back to me for review the same evening, with designs and all."

The guide never needed more effort from her. It needed a system that starts from the last version instead of a blank page.
old_hook: She kept meaning to update a 75-page guide. It never moved.

hook: AI doesn't make your content robotic. Blank chats do.
body:
Give Claude 3 of your real past posts. Ask: "What do you notice about how I write?" Then: "Draft the next one in that voice."

Edit it like any draft. Your voice is the asset. Claude is the assistant.

hook: Most owners blame time. I don't think time is your AI bottleneck.
body:
Which one is it for you?
A) I don't know where to start
B) The answers sound generic
C) I don't trust it yet
D) OK, it's time

Comment your letter. The winner gets the next post.

hook: Your to-do list doesn't need a better app. It needs a cut.
body:
Paste your list into Claude and send: "Group these by effort and impact. Flag what I could delete, delegate or simplify. Then give me a realistic order for the week."

10 minutes on Monday. Fewer tasks, not a prettier list.

hook: You're not behind on AI. You're following too many people.
body:
Every feed shows someone 10 steps ahead with a new tool.

The only AI that matters this month is the one that takes a task off your plate this month. You're allowed to ignore the rest.

hook: 5 extra hours a week won't change anything if you spend them working.
body:
Tell me what you'd do. Rest, sell, create, be home for dinner?

One founder I worked with got roughly 6 hours a week back once her follow-ups ran on their own. That answer is the reason to learn this. Not the tool.
old_hook: Don't tell me what you'd work on with 5 extra hours a week.

hook: Every customer reply you write from scratch is one you've already written.
body:
Send Claude: "Here's a message from a customer: [paste]. Here's how I usually respond: [paste an example]. Draft a reply in my voice, warm and clear, and flag anything I should check before sending."

Claude drafts. You decide. Always read before you send.
old_hook: Stop writing customer replies from a blank screen.

hook: Claude's first draft isn't supposed to be good.
body:
A draft that's 70% right is a head start. Reply: "Here's what's off. Fix it." Then do it again.

Iteration is the skill. Most people stop at round 1 and blame the tool.
old_hook: Quitting after Claude's first draft is the mistake.

hook: You don't need more content ideas. You need fewer, used harder.
body:
Give Claude 1 idea, story or client question. Ask for 3 angles, 3 hooks per angle, and the best format for each.

Pick your favorites, rewrite them in your voice, schedule. 1 idea, a week of posts.

hook: Trying every new AI tool is why none of them stick.
body:
Open Claude at the same time every day for 1 small task.

2 weeks later it's second nature. Consistency beats exploring.
old_hook: You don't need 20 AI tools. You need 1 habit.

hook: "I put this off for a year because it sounded technical."
body:
That's Joan, a clinical researcher. We sat with a pile of her documents and walked her process. By the end of the weekend she was running it on her own. Her words: "Simple, valuable, done."

Overwhelm looks like incompetence. Usually it's missing structure.

hook: 7 things I'd never let Claude do alone.
body:
Final legal wording. Tax decisions. Medical advice. Firing someone. Anything you won't proofread. Replacing your judgment. Sending without reading.

Almost 15 years in compliance taught me this: the tool drafts, the owner decides.

hook: Your saved prompt library is slowing you down.
body:
40 saved prompts, none used. Keep the 3 you'd miss. Delete the rest.

Which 1 would you keep? Share it below.

hook: Stop asking Claude if your plan is good.
body:
You'll hear what you want to hear. Send this instead: "Poke holes in this plan. What am I not seeing? What would a skeptical customer say?"

Better calls come from pushback, and Claude is up at 10pm.

hook: The people getting the most from Claude aren't tech people.
body:
My clients include a business coach, an online seller, a clinical researcher, a boutique studio owner and an independent consultant. None of them code.

What they have is deep knowledge of their own business. Claude organizes what you already know.

hook: "Write me a newsletter" is why your newsletter sounds like everyone's.
body:
Before: "Write me a newsletter."

After: "Write this month's newsletter for [your audience]. Goal: get replies about [your offer]. Tone: warm, direct, no hype. Here's last month's issue so you know my voice: [paste]. Ask me 3 questions first."

Same tool. The difference is context.

hook: Stop planning your AI strategy.
body:
Run 1 small experiment this week. Pick a task. Try it. Notice what happens.

Momentum comes from small tries, not big plans.

hook: Nobody needs your meeting notes. They need what was decided.
body:
Paste your notes into Claude and ask for 3 lists: decisions made, action items with owners, open questions.

Under a minute. Leave out client details you wouldn't share, and check your privacy settings first.
old_hook: Your meeting notes are useless until someone pulls out the decisions.

hook: Every AI tab you have open is a decision you haven't made.
body:
No judgment: how many are open right now? Comment your number.

More than 3? This week's assignment is to close them all and keep the one you use.
old_hook: Close every AI tab you have open. Keep 1.

hook: Her leads lived in her inbox and her memory.
body:
A service-based founder came to me carrying every follow-up in her head. 4 weeks later the full client journey was mapped, the leak points were named, and the follow-up ran on its own. She got roughly 6 hours a week back.

She had me build it. You can learn to build it yourself.

hook: Your overwhelm isn't a skills problem.
body:
It's proof you care about doing this well. Turn that care into a plan: 1 task, 1 prompt, 1 week.

Then adjust. That's the whole method.
old_hook: Overwhelm isn't a flaw. It's proof you care.

hook: Your whole Claude setup should fit on 1 page.
body:
4 parts: your business note, your 3 most-used prompts, 2 examples of your voice, a "never do" list.

Keep it open while you work. Update it monthly. Longer than a page? You're adding, not subtracting.

hook: Using Claude isn't cheating. Doing everything yourself isn't a virtue.
body:
You don't feel guilty using a calculator, an accountant or a template. The thinking, taste and relationships are still yours.

Take the help. Spend the saved time on what only you can do. Where do you draw the line?

hook: Ignore everything else I've posted this month. Do this 1 thing.
body:
Pick 1 task you repeat every week. Write down what a great result looks like. Try it with Claude today.

Then come tell me what happened. I want the wins and the flops.
old_hook: If this feed is the only AI help you get this month, do 1 thing.
